speaker: client
text: He got hit by a car about twenty minutes ago. His name is Diesel. He's five, a German Shepherd.

speaker: tech
text: Triage category red. He's breathing fast, gums are pale.

speaker: dvm
text: Heart rate one sixty, resp rate forty-eight, mucous membranes pale, CRT three seconds. Mentation is quiet but responsive.

speaker: tech
text: Weight thirty-two kilos. Blood pressure systolic eighty.

speaker: dvm
text: Oxygen by flow-by. Place an IV catheter. Give a bolus of lactated Ringer's, ten mils per kilo, over fifteen minutes.

speaker: dvm
text: Methadone, point two milligrams per kilo IV, for pain.

speaker: tech
text: Bolus started at two fifteen. PCV forty-two percent, total solids five point two, lactate four point five.

speaker: dvm
text: AFAST is negative. TFAST shows a small pneumothorax on the right, not enough to tap right now.

speaker: dvm
text: After the bolus, heart rate one twenty and systolic one hundred and ten. Much better.

speaker: dvm
text: He has a right hind laceration and is non weight-bearing on that leg. Radiographs once he's stable.

speaker: client
text: Please do whatever he needs. And if his heart stops, yes, try to bring him back.

speaker: dvm
text: Okay. We'll hospitalise him overnight on fluids and pain relief, and recheck the chest in four hours.
